definitions.gloss: evil spirit, vengeful ghost, supernatural being
definitions.explanation: A malevolent spirit or supernatural entity believed to possess or afflict people, causing illness or misfortune. A concept rooted in classical Japanese literature and folklore.

examples.japanese: {物|もの}の{怪|け}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{取|と}り{憑|つ}かれる→取り憑く：11969_toritsuku⟧。
examples.english: To be possessed by an evil spirit.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{病気|びょうき}→病気：00771_byouki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{物|もの}の{怪|け}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧せいだ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{考|かんが}えた→考える：00856_kangaeru⟧。
examples.english: People in the past attributed illness to evil spirits.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{森|もり}→森：02260_mori⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{物|もの}の{怪|け}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{棲|す}んで⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{言|い}い{伝|つた}え→言い伝え：14145_iitsutae⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There is a legend that supernatural beings dwell in this forest.

notes:
WRITING:
Written as {物|もの}の{怪|け}. The {怪|け} means "strange/mysterious thing."

CULTURAL NOTE:
A key concept in classical Japanese literature, especially in {源氏物語|げんじものがたり} (The Tale of Genji), where {物|もの}の{怪|け} possesses and torments characters. In the Heian period, illness and psychological distress were often attributed to {物|もの}の{怪|け}.

MODERN USAGE:
Widely known today through Studio Ghibli's film 「もののけ⟦{姫|ひめ}→姫：12233_hime⟧」 (Princess Mononoke, 1997). In modern usage, the word evokes an atmospheric, folkloric sense of the supernatural.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {物|もの}の{怪|け}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{取|と}り{憑|つ}かれる→取り憑く：11969_toritsuku⟧ (to be possessed by an evil spirit)
- {物|もの}の{怪|け}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仕業|しわざ}→仕業：10355_shiwaza⟧ (the doing of an evil spirit)
